3. Gold rebounded sharply over the past month after a sharp Q2 reversal from record highs near $5,600 earlier in 2026 and its worst quarterly performance since 2013. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/21/gold-prices-us-debt-dollar.html]

4. A major driver this past month was renewed concern over U.S. fiscal sustainability: government debt topped $40 trillion for the first time, and the Treasury ramped up longer-dated debt buybacks, which pushed Treasury yields and the dollar lower and revived the 'debasement trade' favoring gold. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/21/gold-prices-us-debt-dollar.html]

5. A weaker U.S. dollar and bond market jitters (selloff in longer-dated Treasurys) supported gold demand as an alternative store of value. [https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/gold]

6. Earlier in the month, tamer U.S. inflation data and declining odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike contributed to gold's rally and best week since January. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/gold-prices-metals-fed-rate-hike-inflation.html]

7. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/gold-prices-metals-fed-rate-hike-inflation.html]
